The Committee’s 25 bp cut to a 1.50–1.75% target range, alongside lower IOER and T‑bill purchases/repo operations to maintain ample reserves, is a textbook use of the interest‑rate and liquidity channels to cushion downside risks while inflation runs below target. Research shows business investment is sensitive to financing conditions and internal funds (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994), so easier policy should gradually support capex and inventories even as current business fixed investment and exports remain weak. With market‑based inflation compensation low and core inflation below 2%, New Keynesian frameworks (Galí and Gertler, 1999; Woodford, 2003) justify accommodation to close the output gap and re‑anchor inflation toward target. Transmission lags in the monetary policy channel (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005) imply growth support will materialize over coming quarters rather than immediately. The statement’s emphasis on continued monitoring and the presence of two dissenters underscore residual uncertainty despite solid labor markets and strong household spending. Overall, the literature suggests the action is supportive but cautious, reflecting modest near‑term tailwinds and persistent inflation shortfalls.
